st.headline: ‘All of this is going to pass’: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on AI market turmoil
st.teaser: The Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index fell for eight straight days.
fullText: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang took a sanguine view of the latest AI stock-market rout, saying the benefits of the technology will soon outweigh the concerns of investors.
“All of this is going to pass, and the reason for that is very simple,” Huang told Bloomberg’s Emily Chang during an event in Berlin.

“It’s going to be transformative. It’s going to impact in a very positive way every single industry and every single country. There’s no question it will continue, and we’re at the beginning of that.”
The remarks capped a tumultuous week for shares of chipmakers and AI infrastructure companies.
The closely watched Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index has now fallen for eight straight days, marking the longest losing streak since 2008.
Nvidia shares, meanwhile, have dropped during seven of the past eight sessions. Investors have expressed worry that AI spending is not sustainable at a time of higher borrowing costs.

All the while, Huang has stuck to upbeat predictions for the AI market and its impact on the broader economy. He expects the returns from massive investments in hardware to ultimately ease market jitters.
“With respect to some of the news, it’s choppy news,” he said. “News, as you know, happens all the time, but it won’t change the fundamentals.”
Nvidia is central to the global build-out of artificial intelligence infrastructure.
It is the biggest seller of AI accelerators, chips that are used to develop and run models. And it has branched out into a variety of related hardware, software and services.
The latest sell-off has taken a particular toll on CoreWeave, a cloud-computing services provider that counts Nvidia as one of its biggest backers.
The company’s bonds recently hit levels that typically signal distress, and the stock lost a quarter of its value this week.
Huang has repeatedly encouraged investors to look beyond near-term reports and concentrate on the long-range value of the technology.
“Stay focused on first principles,” he said during the interview. “Stay focused on the fundamentals.” BLOOMBERG

cna.headline: Former Dior Men artistic director Kim Jones is reviving his own label with a Hong Kong flagship
cna.teaser: The British designer is returning to the brand he first launched in 2003, with a new collection due in 2027 and more stores across Asia planned.
fullText: British designer Kim Jones has announced the return of his eponymous label, along with plans to open its first store in Hong Kong.

Jones, who was artistic director of Dior Men from 2018 to early 2025, broke the news earlier this week. According to a brand statement, the label will offer a “broader wardrobe unrestricted by traditional categories”, with apparel made in Japan and leather goods produced in Italy.

His first autumn/winter 2027 collection is slated to launch exclusively online at kimjones.com in mid-2027, while the Hong Kong flagship at Central Yards is scheduled to open in October 2027. More stores across Asia are also in the pipeline.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kim Jones Studio (@kimjonesstudio)

Jones’ social media announcement was met with enthusiasm from fellow designers and celebrities, with Donatella Versace, Marc Jacobs, Matthieu Blazy and David Beckham among those offering their congratulations.

“After many years working with incredible houses and collaborators, it feels like the right moment to do something under my own name again. This brings together the things I’ve always been interested in – fashion, art and design – and gives me the space to work with people I admire and explore new ideas. I’m excited about what comes next,” said Jones.
Further details about the label remain scarce, but interested customers can sign up for early access on the Kim Jones website.

This isn’t the first time Jones has gone solo. His latest venture marks a return to the eponymous label he founded in 2003, after graduating from Central Saint Martins with a master’s degree in fashion. He closed the label five years later when he joined Dunhill as creative director.

In 2011, Jones moved to Louis Vuitton, where he was appointed artistic director of menswear. There, his flair for incorporating streetwear and sportswear influences into luxury craftsmanship and tailoring quickly caught the attention of fashion insiders. He became even more of a household name after orchestrating Louis Vuitton’s 2017 collaboration with popular skatewear brand Supreme, which became a global hit and drew snaking queues – along with some altercations – at its pop-up stores around the world.

Dior Homme brought Jones on board as its artistic director in March 2018, three months after his departure from Louis Vuitton. He rebranded it as Dior Men and reshaped the brand’s vision of menswear by blending its couture heritage with streetwear elements and a softer, more refined approach that challenged conventional notions of masculine dressing.
He also gave Dior Men a dash of pop culture appeal through partnerships with the likes of streetwear icon Shawn Stussy, rapper Travis Scott and artists KAWS (Brian Donnelly) and Daniel Arsham.

Particularly memorable was Jones’ Dior Men debut for spring/summer 2019, which featured a towering 10-metre KAWS BFF sculpture inspired by Christian Dior and covered in thousands of roses and peonies at the centre of the runway. Another highlight was his work with K-pop group BTS, for whom he designed custom stage outfits for their 2019 world tour.
While at Dior Men, Jones also served as artistic director of Fendi’s womenswear, succeeding Karl Lagerfeld in the role. His tenure lasted from 2020 to 2024.

Since leaving Dior in January 2025, Jones has pursued other projects, including a collaboration with luxury lifestyle brand Aman Essentials. He also joined Chinese outerwear company Bosideng as creative director of its premium Areal line.

His influence on fashion has also been recognised with several honours. Jones was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in 2020 and made a Chevalier of the Legion d’honneur, France’s highest order of merit, in 2025.
